Responsibilities

Team Introduction:

We build the next-generation unified Agent system for TikTok's global e-Commerce customer service — running in 30+ languages across one of the largest e-Commerce surfaces on the internet.

Our north star is a self-evolving Agent: post-training, harness, memory / context engineering, tools, and evaluation form one closed loop, and every served conversation becomes the next iteration's training / eval / retrieval / skill-induction signal. This loop is already running in production — cases are mined, root-caused, turned into constrained candidates, replayed against frozen regression sets, and shipped behind guardrails.

Two things make this team different from most "LLM application" work:

We build the agent runtime itself — Codex / Claude-Code-class — not prompts on top of a vendor API.
Evaluation and experimentation are first-class systems, not an afterthought. A self-improving loop optimizes whatever signal you give it, so the hardest and most valuable engineering here is making the judgment trustworthy — not just making the model change.

We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth. Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by the end of the year. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume.

Responsibilities:

Agent runtime (harness / agent loop). Orchestrate skills, tools, and context; implement loop control & intervention, progressive disclosure, and behavior-level guardrails. Build the production safety layer — pre-flight budgets and timeout truncation, serve-time gates, shadow / swap-in answer delivery, and safe fallback paths.
Context & memory for long multi-turn agents. Agentic memory (structured note-taking), context compaction / summarization, context editing / observation masking, and just-in-time (retrieve-then-load) retrieval. Treat context as an evolving, itemized playbook — with structured diffs and a deterministic curator — rather than an ever-growing prompt.
Post-training & the data flywheel. SFT / DPO / RL to internalize rules into weights (so the prompt gets shorter, not longer), plus distillation to smaller serving models. Turn served conversations into training / eval / retrieval signals.
Tools, Skills, and MCP. Tools-as-APIs, connectors, skill / tool search for large inventories, and skill-library governance — description conflicts, trigger evals, cross-skill mis-fire matrices, and on-demand loading instead of dumping every definition into context.
Evaluation you can bet a launch on. LLM-as-judge with human-agreement calibration; statistical rigor — paired comparison, confidence intervals, repeated sampling, pass^k; held-out and time-rolling eval splits with overfitting alarms; cascaded scoring and cross-family judge panels to make evaluation affordable at scale.
The self-evolving loop. Case mining → automatic root-cause → constrained candidate generation → replay verification against frozen regression sets → canary → flywheel. Build the plumbing that makes it auditable: candidate registry with exact runtime read-back, change lineage, and an archive of rejected candidates you can sample from next round.
Online experimentation & causal readout. Shadow / canary / A-B, non-inferiority gates, traffic-split health, metric definitions that survive scrutiny, and off-policy counterfactual evaluation where live A/B isn't possible.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualification(s):

Individuals who are completing or have recently completed a PhD degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics or a related discipline
Strong Python plus one of C++ / Go / Rust / Java
Solid ML / DL / NLP fundamentals, with genuine hands-on experience with LLMs or agents (coursework, research, internship, competition, open-source, or a serious side project)
Basic statistical literacy — you can compute a confidence interval, explain what a p-value does and doesn't mean, and tell the difference between "the number went up" and "the system got better"
Able to read a paper or an engineering blog and turn it into working code

Preferred Qualification(s)

Have built the runtime, not just called an API — even at research / hobby / competition scale: your own agent loop / harness, a memory / context-management system, a RAG or tool-use agent, or a fine-tuned / post-trained model
Hands-on experience in any one of the following — depth in one is enough, breadth welcome:
Post-training: SFT / DPO / RLHF / RLAIF / RLVR, reward modeling, reward hacking and how to defend against it
Agent systems: harness, context engineering, MCP / Skills, sub-agents, tool search
Evaluation & experimentation: LLM-as-judge and judge calibration, pass^k, regression suites, A/B and non-inferiority testing, off-policy evaluation
Self-improving / evolutionary systems: evolutionary program search, candidate archives and parent sampling, automatic prompt / context optimization, multi-objective (Pareto) selection and credit assignment
Inference & serving: vLLM / TensorRT-LLM, MoE, KV / prompt caching, and the cost engineering that comes with it
Multilingual NLP
Publications (for PhD), strong competition results (ACM-ICPC / Kaggle / ML competitions), or notable open-source contributions

About Us

Epia Neuro is a neural technology company developing intent-driven systems designed to restore function and independence for people living with neurological conditions. Its platform integrates implantable neural interfaces, adaptive algorithms, and assistive devices to translate neural intent into real-world action. The company's initial focus is stroke-related motor impairment, with expansion into cognitive decline and other neurological disorders.

The Role

We are generating neural and behavioral data at an increasing pace, across preclinical and early human research studies, with clinical studies ahead. We are looking for a neural data scientist to turn that data into rigorous answers. This ranges from characterizing signal quality and decoding performance to exploring what else our data can tell us, such as which movements and behaviors we can extract and decode. You will design and carry out the analyses and build the analysis workflows that let us do this reliably as our data grows.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor data scientist role on our Research team, reporting to the Director of Research. You will work alongside the scientists running our studies, and your work will shape study design, inform our decoding approaches, and contribute to publications. You will also partner closely with our Software team, which owns production code and the software infrastructure used in our studies.

What You'll Do

Own the analysis of our research studies end to end, from analysis strategy and statistical design through figures, readouts, and publications.
Characterize and validate the in vivo recording performance of our neural interface (signal quality, noise, artifacts, and stability), and establish the preprocessing and quality control that downstream analyses depend on.
Develop and evaluate decoding models that relate neural activity to behavior, including those used in closed-loop study sessions.
Explore neural and behavioral data, including pose estimation and kinematics, to identify new variables and questions worth pursuing.
Build reproducible analysis pipelines and help define data standards across studies.
Work closely with study scientists to shape analysis plans and study design, communicate findings clearly to scientists, engineers, and leadership, and partner with our Software team to hand off research-grade methods and code.

Qualifications

PhD in neuroscience, neural engineering, biomedical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related quantitative field, or a Master's degree in one of these fields with 4+ years of relevant experience in a research-focused role.
Substantial hands-on experience analyzing continuous neural time-series data, ideally field potentials such as ECoG, sEEG, LFP, or EEG.
A strong foundation in neural signal processing, including filtering, spectral analysis (such as band power and time-frequency methods), artifact handling, and feature extraction.
A solid applied machine learning background, including both supervised and unsupervised methods, particularly with noisy biological data.
Demonstrated ability to independently frame scientific questions, select and defend appropriate methods, and carry analyses through to clear conclusions and actionable recommendations.
Experience aligning neural recordings with behavioral and task data.
Strong Python and scientific computing skills, with a track record of writing reusable, maintainable analysis code and using version control and sound data management practices.
Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort working across scientific and engineering teams.

Nice to Have

Experience with human intracranial recordings.
Experience with motor decoding, cognitive-state decoding, or closed-loop BCI.
Experience with video-based pose estimation or kinematic analysis.
Experience building data pipelines or standards shared across studies.
Experience with cloud-based data processing.

How We Work

We are intentional. We prioritize and are thoughtful about how we use others' time.
We care for others. We prioritize safety both for patients and one another.
We own outcomes, not just tasks. Our work demands the highest standards because it impacts real patients and real lives.
Humility is a strength. We are honest about what we know and what we don't know. Getting it right matters more than being right.

Location

This role is based out of the San Francisco Bay Area and is expected to work on site from our Alameda headquarters at least 3 days a week.

Benefits

Full-time employees are eligible for the following benefits:

Competitive base salary with equity
100% of healthcare coverage for you and your dependents
Generous vacation policy
Paid parental leave
Work from our waterfront office in Alameda, CA, with access to collaborative spaces and labs

Compensation Range: $140K - $165K

These are tasks where correctness often can’t be verified automatically, so defining and measuring quality is a core research challenge. You’ll join a small, high-bar team of hands-on engineers and researchers, where each person owns a large part of the work.

The ability to translate ambiguous goals or expert judgment into structured datasets, rubrics, and measurable criteria.

Solution Identification

Solution Development – Applied Research

The Opportunity

Picarro's instruments and analytics power industrial emissions detection, from methane and VOC leak detection to process and emissions monitoring at industrial facilities. We're looking for a Data Scientist who can apply rigorous statistical and physical modeling to Picarro's core measurement challenges: detecting, attributing, localizing, and quantifying trace gases and emissions from complex sensor data.

Work with time-series and geospatial data to build analytical workflows that combine sensor data with atmospheric and geospatial context.
Design and run experimental programs to develop and validate algorithms, deepening our understanding of plume propagation and detection.

Ph.D. or Master's in Physics, Applied Math, Atmospheric or Ocean Science, Astrophysics, Engineering, or a related physical science, or equivalent applied experience.

Hands-on experience with time-series and geospatial data.

You will work alongside other Data Scientists, Product Managers, Designers, Engineers, Architects, and Program Managers to evolve Intuit’s Identity capabilities within Intuit’s Platform. As a key member of the data science team, you will have a strong track record of combining advanced analytical skills with exceptional business and entrepreneurial acumen. You will also have an ownership mindset with a strong willingness to take on new challenges with enthusiasm.

This is an exciting time to join the Identity Data Science Team at Intuit as we are building many new cutting-edge capabilities. These include a next-generation Verified Identity Network, password-less authentication powered through passkeys, Generative AI experiences, modern and sophisticated fraud prevention, centralized user and account management, and much more. Data is central to Intuit’s decision-making process, and data scientists are a critical component to evangelize data-driven decisions as we transform and scale Identity capabilities to power Intuit’s future growth.

Responsibilities

Partner with cross functional teams to drive data-backed decisions and actionable insights
Use a hypothesis-driven approach to drive design, implementation, and analysis of A/B experiments. Then provide executive level recommendations on next steps based on the test results and insights
Communicate analytical findings and recommendations in a clear and concise way to non-technical audiences, both in writing and through oral presentations
Provide guidance and thought leadership to business leaders and stakeholders on how best to harness available data to support business goals
Ensure data collection and data processing is optimized to provide crystal-clear visibility into the impact and value of new initiatives and product releases
Identify opportunities for developing new data sources, and provide technical leadership around making those data sources high-quality and broadly available
Pursue data quality, troubleshoot data anomalies, validate data accuracy, and drive issues to resolution
Share responsibility for owning and maintaining the data science backlog, connecting directly with partners and stakeholders to communicate and align on priorities

Qualifications

5+ years of experience working in web, marketing, product, analytics, or other related data science fields with a strong knowledge of statistics
Exceptional SQL skills and experience working with granular web and native clickstream data
Highly proficient in Tableau, Qliksense, Quicksight or similar software
Exceptional ability to take initiative, be a self-starter, and solve problems
Outstanding communications skills with the ability to influence decision makers and build consensus with stakeholder teams
Proactive and inquisitive learner who seeks out and capitalizes on opportunities for change that enhance the business, rather than reacting to circumstances
Strong organizational skills, time management, accountability, and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously to meet objectives and key deadlines
Love for mentoring and guiding others on best practices. Passionate about the advancement of the whole team
Experience in programming languages, automation tools, and stats packages (e.g. Python) is a plus; comfortable creating re-usable data pipelines

Scale works with the industry’s leading AI labs to provide high quality data and accelerate progress in GenAI research. You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to define best practices in data-driven AI development. Research and develop novel post-training techniques, including SFT, RLHF, and reward modeling, to enhance LLM core capabilities in both text and multimodal modalities.
Design and experiment new approaches to preference optimization.

Publish research findings in top-tier AI conferences.

Ph.D. or Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, or a related field.

Experience with post-training techniques such as RLHF, preference modeling, or instruction tuning.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Published research in areas of machine learning at major conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, CVPR, etc.) and/or journals
Previous experience in a customer facing role.
